sections.text:
يوضح هذا المستند فحص المعدات I1، الذي يجب إجراؤه عليه 
القواعد الأسبوعية كما هو موضح بواسطة W1 في كتلة العنوان.

The IC687 Bus Transmitter Module (BTM) is used in a FIP single 
rack redundancy system. It provides a path for Redundancy communications when 
connected to the Redundancy Communications Module (RCM) in the other half of the 
twosection redundancy rack. Each section of this rack requires a Bus 
Transmitter Module and a Redundancy Communications Module. It also provides a 
high performance parallel interface to the programming device.

The first draft is initiated by eng. Mohamed Tawfeeq, tested by 
eng. Bahaa Abd El-Wahab, revised by MDEPC quality control eng. Adel El Naggar, 
accepted by general manager eng. Mohamed Elshreif, approved by eng. Ahmed Sawan 
head sector of Nubaria power station .

This document certified by eng. Samir Abd El Gillil MDEPC quality 
control general manager and MPIS coordinator and approved by eng. Mohammed Nageb 
quality control head sector.

Two Bus Transmitter Modules required per system (in dual 
 backplane redundancy rack).

Three LED indicators provide module, programmer port, and 
 expansion port status.

No DIP switches to set, easy software configuration into MFC 
 system.

sections.text:
Three green LEDs at top of module provide module status 
information as described below.

The top LED (MODULE OK) LED is ON when the CPU software completes 
its powerup configuration of the BTM, and has polled (or attempted to poll) 
each expansion rack in the system. It is OFF when any of these conditions are 
not met.

The middle LED (Programmer Port Enabled) is the Programmer Port 
Active LED. This LED is either blinking or ON when the programmer and the MFC 
are communicating. It is OFF when they are not communicating. Note that this 
port is not used in communications between the Windows programmer and the PLC.

The bottom LED (Expansion Port Enabled) provides the status of 
the redundancy communications link. This LED is either blinking or ON when the 
BTM is communicating with the Redundancy Communications Module connected to it 
through the IC697CBL803 cable. It is OFF when they are not communicating.

First, make sure rack power is turned off. Then, use a medium-blade, slotted 
 screwdriver to loosen the top and bottom holding screws just enough to free 
 the module from the rack. Note: Screws are held captive in the module, so
